cards.title: The all-channel second-order optimum equals the isometric-orbit value: kappa_opt = 1 - theta = 0.616 +- 0.003 (numerical; conditional on H1, H2, H3)
cards.statement: Phase 5 answer to 'the exact value of the all-channel optimum (non-isometric channels)'. Analytic (rigor/exact_optimum_tangent_problem.tex, refereed, repairs applied): every feasible quasi-free channel is exactly (co-isometry V, isometry loss N = 1 - XX* >= 0, noise 0 <= Y = Z - X Q_BB X* <= N); the leading-order problem is a convex tangent programme, and the isometric-orbit optimum (value (1 - theta) g_Q(deltadot)) is its global optimum iff (a) M_* = Herm((t_* Q)_DD) >= 0 and M_* - tau_* >= 0 (tau_* = (t_*)_DD, as forms) and (e) the one-sided endpoint functional E(zeta) = 2 b(delta_*, A(zeta,0,0)) >= 0 for every admissible (dissipative) isometry generator zeta. For the two model boundary directions, E(zeta_inf) = 2 lambda (1 - theta) g_Q > 0 is proved and E(zeta_0) > 0 is numerical; the reduction of the WHOLE cone of admissible generators to these two directions is proved only for vector fields (Prop 4.10) and is otherwise a declared hypothesis H3 (referee2_exact_optimum_tangent_problem.tex S1: multiplicity > 1 shift semigroups and unbounded skew-adjoint multiplication operators escape the argument). Numerical (F2, rigid parameter-free modular frame with exact Moebius rigidity): (a) holds in the limit (violation lambda_min/||M_*|| = -4.1e-3 ... -3.7e-4 at h = 0.24 ... 0.03, scaling as h^1.15 and 1/Ymax, achievable gain ~ h^1.85 -> 0); (e) on the model cone: E(zeta_inf) > 0 is proved; at zeta_0 the corner term (1/2) M_*(0,0)/h = +10.3, +16.1, +24.7, +37.2 at h = 0.24 ... 0.03 (~h^-0.60, the scheme-invariant continuum quantity; the discrete total +34 ... +258 is upwind-viscosity dominated and is not the margin) diverges, so A(zeta_0,0,0) is not in the form domain, E(zeta_0) = +infinity and (e) is VACUOUS at zeta_0 rather than satisfied with a margin (F1 Rem 4.11(ii), Prop 4.10(5)); no sign change in h, Y, Ymax. Hence, numerically and under H3, non-isometric quasi-free channels (isometry loss, noise, non-surjective isometries) do NOT lower the second-order recovery error: kappa_opt = 1 - theta with theta = 0.384 +- 0.003 (F3, two discretisations reconciled; S10's 0.300 was a taper-suppressed lower bound), i.e. E^(2) = (0.616 +- 0.003) f_2 z^2 per chirality. Conditional on H1 (differentiability along the scaled family), H2 (minimisers within the scaled-family form) and H3 (cone hypothesis) of the F1 document; the unconditional statements remain E_rec <= 0.616 f_2 z^2 (1+o(1)) (E1 upper half for isometric channels + theta) and E_rec >= dual form (optimality_all_channels.tex eq. (10)). Exact fidelity for NON-isometric channels was not needed: the optimum is attained on the isometric orbit, where E1 applies. Open: analytic proof of (a) and (e); H1, H2, H3; closed form of theta (Wiener-Hopf problem, prop:thetaframe); analytic proof that theta > 0 (E_D u E_D not self-adjoint).

cards.title: E_rec <= (1-theta) f2 z^2 (1+o(1)): the zero-collar compression is NOT optimal in exact fidelity
cards.statement: PROVED (no numerical input): per chirality E_rec <= (1 - theta_fr) f2 z^2 (1+o(1)) (Thm 7.3), where theta_fr is the isometric-orbit gain sup over FINITE-RANK anti-self-adjoint G = E_D G E_D with v_G != 0; and theta_fr > 0 iff R_a != 0, equivalently (S10 Cor. 11.2: E_D u E_D is purely anti-self-adjoint) iff E_D u E_D != 0. Proof: the g_Q-free (UH) (card uhlmann-upper-half-proved) minimised in lambda and maximised in G, plus ||u||_2^2 = g_B/4 (S10 Prop. 4.3(2)) so (1/2)||u||^2 = f2. NUMERICAL: theta_fr >= 0.38, hence kappa_opt <= 0.616 +- 0.003 < 1, i.e. the zero-collar compression is beaten in EXACT fidelity, not merely in the second-order functional. The bridge from the published theta to theta_fr is Remark 7.4: (i) theta_fr = theta_HS by S_2-density of finite-rank anti-Hermitian G supported in D (all quantities depend on G only through P^perp G P, S_2-continuously), only theta_HS = theta (bounded G with P^perp G P in S_2 but G not in S_2) is open and is irrelevant for a LOWER bound; (ii) the explicit admissible HS direction G = R_a gives theta_fr >= 0.0143; (iii) every discretisation behind the numerical theta is finite-dimensional, so its optimisers are finite rank -- and F3's extrapolations are themselves taken over finite meshes, so theta_fr >= 0.38 is as well supported as theta = 0.384 +- 0.003 (Phase 5, F3, card theta-value; the modular Galerkin frame of S12 Sec. 5.2 and the parameter-free modular Wiener-Hopf frame of rigor/exact_optimum_tangent_problem.tex Prop 6.2 agree to 3e-4 after extrapolation; S10 Sec. 7's 0.300 +- 0.005 is a taper-suppressed LOWER bound). Wording updated in rigor/exact_fidelity_upper_half.tex Remark 7.4 (rem:thetafr) and the dated addendum to its Sec. 10. Sandwich (Cor 7.5): sup over admissible test families of liminf Delta_z(t_z)^2/(8 V(t_z) z^2) <= liminf E_rec/z^2 <= limsup E_rec/z^2 <= (1 - theta_fr) f2; the identification of the left side with D_z = min_F g_Q is S12 Thm 4.1(2) and is CONDITIONAL on a test family with ||t_z||_1^2/V(t_z) bounded and Delta_z(t_z)||t_z||_1/V(t_z) -> 0. Also note (referee R7): the structural chain is duality-free but the constant f2 reaches back to PA Prop. 7.6, hence to twisted duality.

cards.title: The compression is not the minimiser of the second-order functional
cards.statement: E_D u E_D != 0: composing the compression with a Bogoliubov rotation e^{-eps G*} inside B lowers g_Q by the factor 1 - theta, theta = 0.384 +- 0.003 (Phase 5 track F3, card theta-value, numerics/optimality_all/F3_RESULTS.md). The two published discretisations are reconciled, not in conflict: S10's spectral-model theta = 0.300(5) is a taper-suppressed LOWER bound (the smoothstep ultraviolet taper on the spectral derivative removes modes carrying ~20% of theta; there is no taper-free lattice limit because of the second Fermi point, and theta_circ rises linearly in log L, so the 1/L Richardson extrapolation used the wrong variable), while the modular Galerkin model's 0.29 -> 0.34 (increasing with resolution) extrapolates to the same 0.384 as the parameter-free modular Wiener-Hopf frame (agreement 3e-4 after extrapolation, measured order h^0.77). Hence min_F g_Q <= (1 - theta) f2 z^2 = (0.616 +- 0.003) f2 z^2, no dual certificate for f2 z^2 exists, and S8's 'consistent with optimal' is superseded at this level. theta > 0 is numerical, not proved.

cards.title: Corner calculus: sequential one-sided recovery = Schwarzian point masses at the junctions
cards.statement: One-sided zero-collar protocol on adjacent intervals A_1..A_n: step m adjoins A_new to the block J_{m-1} conditioning on a sub-block A_B adjacent to it, corner p^(m) = the end of A_B not shared with A_new, parabolic compression toward p^(m) with sigma_m = s_m/(l_B+l_new), s_m in [lambda_m, 2 lambda_m] (each step is the VACUUM Petz map of its own inclusion F(A_B) subset F(A_B u A_new), applied to whatever state the earlier steps produced); composite point map Phi = k_1 o ... o k_N (first step OUTERMOST). (1) GENERAL RULE, no hypothesis (Thm 5.2): Phi is C^1 piecewise-Moebius and S(Phi) = -2 sum_m sigma_m G_m'(x_m) delta_{x_m} -- with the DERIVATIVE G_m'(x_m), not G_m(x_m) -- where G_m := k_{m+1} o ... o k_N and x_m := G_m^{-1}(p^(m)); terms with p^(m) outside the range of G_m are absent (the corner is swallowed). (2) UNDER (H) (no earlier corner lies in the interior of a later step moving part A_B u A_new) (Thm 5.3): S(Phi) = -2 sum_k kappa_k delta_{p_k} over the INTERIOR junctions of J_N, kappa_k = sum of the sigmas of the steps whose corner is p_k; in particular S(Phi) is order independent. Sufficient for (H): (a) every A_B is a SINGLE chain interval AND the starting block has >= 2 chain intervals; (b) all corners coincide (VWZ 1(B)); (c) N = 1. CORRECTION (G1a): single-interval conditioning ALONE does not imply (H) -- Example 5.6, chain (1,1,1) started from the single interval A_2, add A_3 on A_2 then A_1 on A_2: the first corner is swallowed (not in the range of k_2), S(Phi) = -2 sigma_2 delta_{p_3} and Phi = (global Moebius) o k_2, so the first step leaves the state unchanged. (3) The composite algebra map is a normal *-isomorphism onto its range (Note 4 Thm 7.1 per step; Phi itself is NOT a single zero-collar map) and equals beta_{V_Phi} (V_{k_1}V_{k_2} = V_{k_1 o k_2}); the recovered state depends on Phi ONLY through S(Phi), because equal Schwarzians means Phi_2 = g o Phi_1 with g a global Moebius map (without pole on the OPEN interval Phi_1(J); the closure version is false) and omega o Ad U_g = omega (Thm 6.3). For a single corner the state, hence Phi_A, depends only on zeta = sigma beta_I(p) and not on the side of the compression (Cor 6.5). (4) RIGIDITY (Thm 7.3): omega o beta_Phi = omega on F(I) iff Phi is Moebius iff S(Phi) = 0; since all Schwarzian masses are negative and the last step is never swallowed, exact recovery never occurs for a protocol WHOSE LAST STEP KEEPS A NON-EMPTY PART (A_B strictly inside the block) -- unconditionally, without the second-order law. The hypothesis is needed: a degenerate step conditioning on the WHOLE block puts its corner on the boundary of I, where beta_I = 0, and is a pure Moebius compression that recovers the vacuum exactly (Rem 7.4; it is not a recovery in the Petz sense, since it keeps nothing fixed). (5) Consequences: VWZ 1(B) = 1(A) LITERALLY as point maps and for every common rotation t (2c/(b(b+c)) + 2d/((b+c)(b+c+d)) = 2(c+d)/(b(b+c+d))); VWZ Protocol 3 in either order is literally the same point map (parabolic L and R at the same point commute) and equals, up to post-composition with a global Moebius map, the over-compressed Theorem-A step with kept block AB, conditioning interval C, new interval D and s = (sigma_1+sigma_2)(c+d) > 2 lambda = 2d/c STRICTLY, hence Phi^(3) = Phi_A(zeta_eff), zeta_eff = (sigma_1+sigma_2)(a+b)(c+d)/(a+b+c+d); protocols with the same corner measure give the same state; and with single-interval conditioning the corner measure -- hence the holonomy -- depends only on the STARTING BLOCK, so the 2^{n-2} protocols starting from an adjacent pair fall into exactly n-1 classes, distinct pairs giving distinct measures (Prop 9.1 + Lem 9.2; tables for n = 4 and n = 5).

cards.title: The universal corner-correlation kernel Ghat(Delta): closed form, positivity, decay

cards.title: Separation constraint: all-weak L->R Petz chains have e^{Delta_k} >= 2/eps (sharp)
cards.statement: L->R ordinary-Petz chain (start A_1A_2, adjoin A_{k+1} conditioning on A_k), corners p_2..p_{n-1}, kappa_k = 2 l_{k+1}/(l_k(l_k+l_{k+1})), zeta_k = kappa_k L_{k-1}(T-L_{k-1})/T, Delta_k = y_{k+1}-y_k the modular length of A_k (Delta_n := +infinity). EXACT IDENTITIES (Lem 10.3): zeta_k = sinh(Delta_{k+1}/2)/(sinh(Delta_k/2) sinh((Delta_k+Delta_{k+1})/2)), equivalently 1/zeta_k = sinh^2(Delta_k/2) coth(Delta_{k+1}/2) + (1/2) sinh(Delta_k) -- the corner strengths are functions of the MODULAR LENGTHS alone; consequently e^{Delta_k} <= 1 + 2/zeta_k, with equality IF AND ONLY IF k = n-1 (where Delta_n = infinity and coth = 1) and strict inequality for k <= n-2, the exact gap being 2 sinh^2(Delta_k/2)(coth(Delta_{k+1}/2) - 1); and (e^{Delta_k}-1) zeta_k = 2 r_k(1+v_k)/(1+r_k) >= 2 r_k/(1+r_k) (REF-P6-0 item 6). SEPARATION THEOREM (Thm 11.1): if zeta_j <= eps < 2 for every corner j >= k (only the corners to the RIGHT of p_k are used), then e^{Delta_k} >= 2/eps, and e^{Delta_{n-1}} >= 1 + 2/zeta_{n-1} >= 1 + 2/eps for the last corner. Proof: with gamma_j := coth(Delta_j/2) - 1 = 2/(e^{Delta_j}-1), the identity gives e^{Delta_j} >= 1 + 4/(zeta_j (2 + gamma_{j+1})), hence the recursion gamma_j <= zeta_j(1 + gamma_{j+1}/2); downward induction from gamma_n = 0 gives the fixed point gamma_j <= 2 eps/(2-eps), and substituting back gives e^{Delta_k} >= 1 + (4/eps)/(2 + 2 eps/(2-eps)) = 2/eps. SHARPNESS: only as eps -> 0. REF-P6-3 computed the EXACT constrained minimum of e^{Delta_k} by a closed backward recursion in the modular variables: 6.8134, 20.0499, 66.6817, 200.0050, 666.6682 at eps = 0.3, 0.1, 0.03, 0.01, 0.003, i.e. (eps/2) min = 1.0220, 1.0025, 1.00022, 1.000025, 1.000002 -- the bound is exceeded by 2.2% at eps = 0.3 and is approached only as eps -> 0. REF-P6-0s eps = 0.3 entry 6.75 lies BELOW the exact minimum 6.8134 and is a float-cancellation artifact (a naive search over the lengths destroys T - L_k); it is withdrawn. The hypothesis cannot be weakened to the pair {k,k+1}: with only that pair weak the separation stays O(1) (min e^{Delta} = 8.07 at eps = 0.01, REF-P6-3). GENERAL ADMISSIBLE CASE (Cor 11.2): with s_j in [lambda_j, 2 lambda_j], zeta_j <= eps < 1 for all j >= k gives e^{Delta_k} >= 1/eps.

cards.title: Exact -1/2 log det(1-V^*V) with the optimised extension confirms (UH) beyond first order
cards.statement: With the Tikhonov-optimised exterior generator Z_e (mu = 1e-8; the mu = 1e-4 rows overshoot by 3e-3 and are not used) and W~ = exp(Z_pre + Z_e), Z_pre = -s D_chi resp. -s(D_chi + eps_* G_*), the EXACT Uhlmann exponent UH = -(1/2) log det(1 - V^*V), V = P^perp W~ P (singular values, log1p), satisfies at L = 128..384 and s = 0.001, 0.002, 0.005: UH_compr / ((1/2) s^2 |u|^2) between 1.00000 (s = 0.001) and 0.99981 (s = 0.005, L = 384), i.e. equal to the first-order UB to within 2e-4, the deficit a clean O(s^2); UH_rot / ((1/2) s^2 |u|^2) = 0.70885 (L=128), 0.71125 (192), 0.71057 (256), 0.70764 (384) at s = 0.001, against 1 - theta = 0.70890, 0.71120, 0.71051, 0.70767: agreement to about 5e-5, i.e. four significant digits; decreasing slightly with s (0.70714 at s = 0.005, L = 384). The two second-order-inequivalent constructions exp(Z_pre) exp(Z_e) and W_s exp(-s eps_* G_*) exp(Z_e) give values below the sum version (0.70596 and 0.70810 at L = 128, s = 0.001). Hence (UH) holds in this model beyond first order, with room to spare.

cards.title: NS-circle model: Ext = N^perp exactly, with the dimension identity (L-|I|)^2
cards.statement: In S10's spectral NS-circle model (exact Hardy projection P of rank k = L/2, I = A u D an arc of m = |I| sites, m > L/2) both spanning maps are DIAGONALISED exactly: with Q = E_I P E_I (eigenvalues q, basis U) one has E_I(P^perp l P + P l P^perp)E_I = (1-Q) l Q + Q l (1-Q), so ||P^perp l P||_2^2 = (1/2) sum_ij den_ij |l_ij|^2 with den_ij = q_i(1-q_j)+q_j(1-q_i); likewise for Z anti-Hermitian on I^c with Qc = E_{I^c} P E_{I^c}. Hence dim_R N = m^2 - 2 z^2 with z = m - L/2 (rank Q = rank(1-Q) = L/2 forces z exact zero and z exact unit eigenvalues, and den vanishes exactly on the (0,0) and (1,1) pairs), dim_R S_2(PH,P^perp H) = L^2/2, and dim_R N^perp = L^2/2 - m^2 + 2z^2 = (L/2 - z)^2 = (L-m)^2 = dim_R Ext. Together with L1 (Ext subset N^perp) this gives Ext = N^perp EXACTLY at every L. Brute-force verification with explicit real bases at L = 32, 48: ranks 316/196 and 711/441 match the formula exactly and all principal angles between Ext and N^perp are 0 (cos = 1.0000000000 to 10 digits); at L = 64 double precision loses 22 of 1319 dimensions of N to roundoff but all principal angles are still 0.

cards.statement: R := ||M||^2 - ||Pi M||^2 - ||Proj_Ext M||^2 = dist((1-Pi)M, Ext)^2, recomputed in mpmath from the closed forms P_jk = (1/L) sum_{n<L/2} w^{n(j-k)} and d_jk = (1/L) sum_n i nu_n s_n w^{n(j-k)}: R = -6.5e-60 (L=32, 60 dps), -2.5e-56 (L=48, 60 dps), +6.7e-72 (L=64, 80 dps), against ||(1-Pi)M||^2 = 4.4e-2, 3.0e-2, 2.6e-2. cards.title: Optimised exterior extension: UB_c = (1/2)s^2|u|^2 exactly and UB_rot/UB_c = 1-theta
cards.statement: In the NS-circle model (a = 2, Lg = 1, uv = (0.30,0.42), alpha = 3) with the exterior generator OPTIMISED (least squares over all anti-Hermitian Z_e supported on I^c, solved in closed form by the Qc-eigenbasis diagonalisation): UB(X) = (1/2) dist(X, Ext)^2 = (1/2)(||Pi X||^2 + dist((1-Pi)X, Ext)^2). Numerically dist((1-Pi)M, Ext)^2 and dist((1-Pi)v, Ext)^2 are at roundoff (|d^2| <= 1.3e-10 against ||(1-Pi)M||^2 = 2.45e-2, relative distance <= 1.2e-5 and usually exactly 0 in double precision) for L = 128, 192, 256, 384. UB is exactly quadratic in s, so the ratios are s-independent to machine precision (checked at s = 0.001, 0.002, 0.005). eps_* = -1.0000 in units of s, as predicted by <u,v_x> = ||v_x||^2 = <b,x>.

cards.statement: ANSWERED 2026-09-15 (Phase 4): yes, modulo one numerical input. cards.title: Exterior directions exhaust the invisible space: closure(Ext) = N^perp (question (Q) settled, YES)
cards.statement: In the real Hilbert space S_2(PH, P^perp H) with inner product Re Tr(X^* Y), let N = {P^perp l P : l = l^* = E_I l E_I} (visible space) and Ext = {P^perp Z_e P : Z_e^* = -Z_e = E_{I^c} Z_e E_{I^c}} (exterior directions). Then closure(Ext) = N^perp = {B : E_I(B + B^*)E_I = 0}, and finite-rank Z_e already suffice. Proof (invariant, no Halmos normal form): B orthogonal to both spaces means, with Xi := B + B^*, Gamma := 2P-1: Gamma Xi + Xi Gamma = 0, E_I Xi E_I = 0, E_{I^c} Gamma Xi E_{I^c} = 0. Compressing Gamma Xi Gamma = -Xi with E_{I^c} and inserting 1 = E_I + E_{I^c} twice gives Gamma' pi Gamma' = pi with pi = E_{I^c} Xi E_{I^c}, Gamma' = E_{I^c}(2P-1)E_{I^c}; since Gamma' is a self-adjoint contraction with no eigenvalue +-1 (generic position) Gamma'^n -> 0 strongly, and pi is compact, so pi = 0; then E_{I^c} P E_I (E_I Xi E_{I^c}) = 0 with E_{I^c} P E_I injective gives Xi = 0. FINITE-RANK exterior generators already suffice (closure(Ext_fr) = closure(Ext) = N^perp). Compactness of the test element is NOT needed (referee R3): for any BOUNDED pi with pi = Gamma'^n pi Gamma'^n one has |<xi, pi eta>| <= ||Gamma'^n xi|| ||pi|| ||Gamma'^n eta|| -> 0, so pi = 0 by two-sided strong convergence alone; the earlier claim that bounded solutions exist (from approximate eigenvectors) is false, since approximate eigenvectors at +-1 tend weakly to 0. Generic position IS essential: one failure in each of the two groups breaks it (f in h_{I^c} cap PH and g in h_I cap P^perp H give B = |g><f| nonzero in N^perp cap Ext^perp). Only a CLOSURE is claimed because Z_e -> P^perp Z_e P has unbounded inverse on N^perp (E2 Sec. 2.3), not because of the fixed-point equation. Second, independent proof: N and Ext are the (1,1)-sector standard subspaces of F(I) and F(I)', so (Q) IS Haag/twisted duality (Tomita: K^perp_R = i K').
cards.verify: rigor/exact_fidelity_upper_half.tex Sec. 5 (Lemma 5.1 generic position, Thm 5.3 invariant proof, Thm 5.4 duality (which, for a bounded interval, uses twisted duality for the disconnected complement plus additivity, circle picture) proof); numerically corroborated by E0 card finite-dim-exterior-density.

cards.title: Finite chains: exterior directions span exactly the invisible space (Ext = N^perp)
cards.statement: On the half-filled hopping chain with P the Fermi projection and I a contiguous block (n = 8..16, |I| = 3..7), the real span N of the visible directions P^perp l P (l Hermitian on I) has dimension |I|^2, the span Ext of the exterior directions P^perp Z P (Z anti-Hermitian on I^c) is orthogonal to N and has dimension 2k(n-k) - |I|^2, and N + Ext is all of S_2(PH, P^perp H): Ext = N^perp exactly in every case. Algebraically, B = P^perp X P is orthogonal to N iff E_I(B + B^*)E_I = 0 and to Ext iff E_{I^c}(B - B^*)E_{I^c} = 0; with H = B + B^* (Hermitian, P-off-diagonal) and S = 1 - 2P one has B - B^* = S H, so (Q) is the two-projection statement: a P-off-diagonal Hermitian H with E_I H E_I = 0 and E_{I^c} S H E_{I^c} = 0 vanishes. This is the finite-dimensional shadow of question (Q) of the Phase 4 brief; the continuum statement (density, Hardy projection, interval) is track E1's target.

cards.title: Amplification: the corner strength in the chain frame is zeta_step (1 + z')
cards.statement: For a corner (p, sigma) and two intervals I_step subset I containing p, the strengths zeta^(I') = sigma beta_{I'}(p) (beta_{I'}(x) = (x-alpha)(omega-x)/(omega-alpha), the modular-frame density of I' = (alpha,omega)) satisfy zeta^(I) >= zeta^(I_step), with equality iff I = I_step, because beta_{(alpha,omega)}(p) is increasing in omega and decreasing in alpha. If the step's kept block reaches the left end of the chain, I_step = (p_1, f) with f the far end of the moving part, then zeta^(I)/zeta^(I_step) = beta_I(p)/beta_{I_step}(p) = (a+b)(b+c)/(b(a+b+c)) = 1 + z' with a = p - p_1, b = f - p, c = p_{n+1} - f; z' = ac/(b(a+b+c)) is simultaneously the cross ratio of (p_1, p, f, p_{n+1}) and paper 1's Markov variable z of the coarse triple (kept block | A_B u A_new | rest of the chain). z' >= 0, and z' = 0 iff f = p_{n+1}, i.e. iff the step is the last one. Underlying exact fact (Lem 3.3, 3.4): the parabolic parameter is a (-1)-density, sigma' = sigma/M'(p) under a Moebius change of coordinate, so zeta = sigma beta_I(p) is Moebius invariant and is exactly the coefficient of w(y-y_p) = -4 sinh^2((y-y_p)/2) 1_{y>y_p} in the first-order field in the modular frame of I; for I = (-a,L), p = 0, sigma = s/L it is paper 1's zeta = as/(a+L).

cards.title: Full primal SDP over F in the modular Galerkin frame: min_F g_Q = 8.41 and 7.13 times g_Q(delta_c) at h = 0.4, 0.3 -- the S11 representability obstruction, not a statement about non-isometric channels
cards.statement:
In the block-exact modular Galerkin frame of kkt_continuum.py (a = 1, L = 2, Lambda = 12, s = 0.1, kind = 'first'), the full primal SDP over F = {X : h_B -> h_D, Z = Z* : X Q_BB X* <= Z <= 1 - X(1-Q_BB)X*} was solved at two rungs (f2_galerkin_a.out; 9425 s at h = 0.4, 24923 s at h = 0.3):
h = 0.4, N = 69, (nA,nB,nC) = (30,9,30): g_Q(delta_c) = 8.1495e-06 = 0.8687 f2 zeta^2, theta = 0.28578, min_F g_Q = 6.8546e-05, min_F/g_Q(delta_c) = 8.411034, ||1 - X X*||_F = 5.872, tr(1 - X X*) = 35.16 of m = 39, ||Z - X Q_BB X*||_F = 3.556, sv(X) in [0.0061, 0.9999];
h = 0.3, N = 91, (nA,nB,nC) = (40,11,40): g_Q(delta_c) = 8.4021e-06 = 0.8956 f2 zeta^2, theta = 0.29926, min_F g_Q = 5.9870e-05, min_F/g_Q(delta_c) = 7.125692, ||1 - X X*||_F = 6.780, tr(1 - X X*) = 46.71 of m = 51, sv(X) in [0.0002, 0.9999].
Both rungs land a factor 7-8 ABOVE the compression defect, not below the isometric-orbit value, and the optimal X is a strong contraction, nothing like a co-isometry.
WHAT IS BEING COMPARED (do not over-read the ratio): min_F g_Q is an exact finite-s minimum over the discretised F, whereas theta, 1 - theta and g_Q(delta_c) on the same rung are FIRST-ORDER (tangent) reference numbers produced by orbit_theta() (the CG of theta_galerkin.py, which it reproduces exactly: 1 - theta = 0.71422 at h = 0.4 and 0.70074 at h = 0.3 against the published 0.714 and 0.701). The two are not values of one and the same programme -- they are computed in one script and share Q and delta_c, but not the same optimisation -- so the ratio must not be read as "the orbit beaten or not beaten by that factor".
WHAT THE RUNGS DO SHOW is the S11 representability obstruction (rigor/sdp_certificate_numerics.tex l.484-497): in a finite Galerkin cell frame the Moebius compression is not representable at all (its V maps cells to non-cells), so the discretised F does not contain the compression point, and min_F g_Q is dominated by that representation error rather than by the physics of non-isometric channels.
H-TREND: the two rungs move in the right direction at fixed Lambda and collar, 8.411034 (h = 0.4) -> 7.125692 (h = 0.3). Two points are a trend, not a verdict, and no extrapolated "factor still to be closed" is claimed. The earlier runs kc_h04.out and kc_h05.out (8.2635 and 10.0467) are NOT comparable rungs of the same ladder: they differ in LamC (6 and 4 vs 12), n_B (9 and 7 vs 9 and 11) and n_C (15 and 8 vs 30 and 40); S11 identifies n_B/n_C and the collar s, not h alone, as the knobs, and kc_h04.out's Delta/(2 g_Q) = -10.325 is S11's n_B < n_C corner.
CONCLUSION: this test cannot decide whether non-isometric channels beat the isometric orbit; the tangent (first-order) problem is the right place to ask, and it is answered in the card kkt-noise-criterion-numerics.

cards.title: Exact KKT certificate at the compression; Moebius rigidity
cards.statement: In the continuum V_c: h_D -> h_B is unitary, both LMIs are active, and the multipliers are unique: Sigma_1 = t_DA Q_AB V_c - t_DD V_c*(1-Q_BB)V_c; the compression maximises Tr(t Q_rec) over F iff Sigma_1 = Sigma_1* >= 0 and Sigma_1 + t_DD >= 0 (necessary and sufficient, no constraint qualification). Legendre reduction V(t) = ||P^perp t P||^2; the DD block of the first-order compression defect vanishes (Moebius generator commutes with P and is local), so the certificate at t_c exists iff E_D u E_D = 0.

cards.title: KKT criterion numerics: every finite run FAILS (a); the violation extrapolates to 0^- as h -> 0, Ymax -> inf; E(zeta_0) > 0 and E(zeta_inf) > 0, so (e) holds for the whole cone under H3
cards.statement:
Numerical evaluation of the F1 Thm 4.4 criterion for the tangent problem (orbit = global optimum iff (a) M_* >= 0 and M_* - tau_* >= 0, and (e) the endpoint functional E(zeta_0) >= 0; t_* is the SLD normalised by g_Q(delta_*) = (1/4) Tr(t_* delta_*), tau_* = E_D t_* E_D, M_* = Herm((t_* Q)_DD)). READ THE SIGN CLAIM AS AN EXTRAPOLATION: at every finite discretisation the run prints "CRITERION (M>=0 and M-tau>=0): False" (f2_t4_h024.out l.4, f2_t4_hladder.out l.5 and l.14, f2_t4_h003.out l.5, every Ymax row of f2_t4_ymax12.out); what the numerics establish is that the violation scales to zero in the double limit, with clean power laws, while the endpoint functional is positive with a large margin on the two model boundary directions (condition (e) for the whole cone then follows only under F1's model-cone hypothesis H3).
(1) PRIMARY FRAME, parameter-free modular Wiener-Hopf (F1 Prop 6.2 as built by F3 in f3_t0.py; I = (-inf,1), y = -log(1-x), A = {y<0}, D = {y>0}, Q exact in the cell basis, ddot in closed form, Moebius rigidity EXACT: ||ddot_DD|| = 0 identically). Structural checks all pass: SLD identity (1/4)Tr(t_* delta_*)/g_Q(delta_*) = 1.0000000000; ||AntiHerm((t_* Q)_DD)||/||M_*|| = 2.8e-9, 8.5e-8, 1.5e-7, 3.5e-7 at h = 0.24, 0.12, 0.06, 0.03; F1's derivative formula d g_Q = (1/2)[Tr(N1 M_*) - Tr(Y1 tau_*)] verified by central finite differences to <= 3e-8 (measured relative errors 3.94e-10, 7.56e-09, 1.08e-08, 2.63e-08 at h = 0.24, 0.12, 0.06, 0.03); theta reproduces F3's ladder (0.31367, 0.34236, 0.35934, 0.36945 at h = 0.24, 0.12, 0.06, 0.03, Y = Ymax = 10).
(a) SCALING OF THE VIOLATION. h-ladder at Y = Ymax = 10: lam_min(M_*)/||M_*|| = -4.076e-3, -1.859e-3, -8.228e-4, -3.667e-4 at h = 0.24, 0.12, 0.06, 0.03 (ratios 2.19, 2.26, 2.24 per halving, i.e. ~ h^1.15), and lam_min(M_* - tau_*) equals lam_min(M_*) to 5 digits (same eigenvector, <p,M_*p> ~ -<p,tau_*p>). Outer-cutoff scan at h = 0.12, Y = 6: lam_min(M_*)/||M_*|| = -3.014e-3, -2.286e-3, -1.865e-3, -1.339e-3, -9.459e-4, -6.360e-4 for Ymax = 6, 8, 10, 14, 20, 30, i.e. lam_min/||M_*|| * Ymax = -0.0181, -0.0183, -0.0186, -0.0187, -0.0189, -0.0191 (~ 1/Ymax), and the rank-one gain Delta^2/g_Q(eta) in units of g_Q(ddot) = 3.325e-4, 1.874e-4, 1.230e-4, 6.236e-5, 3.080e-5, 1.380e-5 with gain * Ymax^2 = 0.0120 ... 0.0124 (~ 1/Ymax^2); on the h-ladder the same gain is 3.85e-4, 1.23e-4, 3.51e-5, 9.69e-6 (~ h^1.85). So lam_min(M_*)/||M_*|| ~ -c(h)/Ymax with c(0.24) = 0.041, c(0.12) = 0.0187 (c ~ h^1.1), and the gain ~ c'(h)/Ymax^2 with c'(0.24) = 0.039, c'(0.12) = 0.0123: both -> 0 in the double limit h -> 0, Ymax -> infinity, i.e. lam_min -> 0^- (a marginal, not a strict, sign). The violating eigenvector p supports this reading: in the Ymax scans at fixed h it is a delocalised mode at y ~ (0.4-0.6) Ymax, tracking the artificial outer end of the y window (the moving endpoint x = 1); the A-side cutoff is irrelevant (Y = 6, 10, 14 give lam_min/||M_*|| = -4.0904e-3, -4.0756e-3, -4.0751e-3 at h = 0.24, Ymax = 10; f2_t4_h024.out and the Y-scan block of f2_t5_endpoint.out). At fixed Ymax = 10 the mode moves inward as h falls (y ~ 5.5, 5.1, 4.3, 1.9) while its eigenvalue keeps shrinking; the two vanishing scalings, not the location, carry the conclusion.
(e) ENDPOINT CONDITION (T5, f2_t5_endpoint.out). E(zeta) = 2 b(delta_*, A(zeta,0,0)) = (1/2)Tr(t_* A(zeta,0,0)) with A from F1 eq:Ablocks. Convention check, exact to machine precision at all four h: E(zeta_inf)/g_Q(ddot) = (1/2)Tr(t_* ddot)/g_Q(ddot) = 1.37265519, 1.31527744, 1.28132522, 1.26109076 against the proved 2(1-theta) = same to 2e-16..1e-15. For zeta_0 = -E_D d/dy E_D discretised on the uniform D-mesh, only the backward (upwind) difference is the admissible shift semigroup (sigma = Herm(zeta_0) <= 0); it gives a TOTAL E(zeta_0)/g_Q(ddot) = +34.122, +66.873, +131.298, +257.998 at h = 0.24, 0.12, 0.06, 0.03, but that total is the scheme-DEPENDENT quantity: the discrete boundary form decomposes as E(zeta_0) = (1/2)[M_*(0,0) + h Tr((-Laplacian) M_*) + M_*(Ymax,Ymax)] and the total (~ h^-0.97) is dominated by the O(h) upwind-viscosity middle term, an artefact of the difference scheme. The scheme-invariant piece, and the only one that converges to F1's continuum boundary form, is the CORNER row (1/2)(M_*)_00/h = +10.304, +16.096, +24.672, +37.210 (~ h^-0.60); it is the continuum margin quoted below. The centred difference is exactly anti-Hermitian (sigma = 0, lies in L-bar) and gives E = 0 to 2e-5; the forward difference has sigma >= 0 (decompression, inadmissible) and gives the negative of the backward value. Both quantities saturate in Ymax (E_bwd = +66.90, +67.07, +67.23, +67.36, +67.45 and corner = +16.46, +16.15, +16.03, +15.96, +15.89 for Ymax = 6, 10, 14, 20, 30 at h = 0.12) and are independent of Y (+67.07, +66.87, +66.87 for Y = 6, 10, 14). The corner term does NOT saturate in h (it grows like h^-0.6), i.e. M_*(y,y) diverges as y -> 0+ and E(zeta_0) = +infinity in the continuum -- a fortiori >= 0. Cross-check (ii): the first-cell diagonal of M_*/h is +0.160, +0.261, +0.409, +0.623 (same sign as E(zeta_0)) and the last-cell diagonal is +3.2e-3, +3.9e-3, +4.4e-3 (same sign as the proved E(zeta_inf) > 0). VERDICT ON (e), QUALIFIED: numerically E(zeta_0) > 0 and E(zeta_inf) > 0, i.e. (e) is verified for the TWO MODEL boundary directions of F1 Prop 4.10(3) -- continuum margin +10.3, +16.1, +24.7, +37.2 g_Q(ddot) (the corner row) at h = 0.24, 0.12, 0.06, 0.03, with no sign change at any h, Y, Ymax, and E(zeta_inf) = 2(1-theta) g_Q(ddot) > 0 exactly. The sign of E(zeta_0) is structurally forced in this frame because -2 sigma >= 0 is a legitimate N_1 direction, so E(zeta_0) = (1/2)Tr((-2 sigma) M_*) >= 0 follows from M_* >= 0. Condition (e) for the WHOLE admissible cone follows from these two numbers only under the model-cone reduction -- F1's hypothesis (H3 in Sec. 4; Prop 4.10(3) and (5)) that modulo L-bar the cone of admissible isometry generators is generated by zeta_0 and zeta_inf -- which is a hypothesis, not something these numerics test. So: numerically (a) in the limit; E(zeta_0) > 0 and E(zeta_inf) > 0; (e) for the whole cone under H3.
CAVEAT ON THE PRIMARY FRAME. It needs no weight cap at the h computed, but the weights are not bounded uniformly in h: kappa_max = 5.38, 6.51, 7.66, 8.84 and max w = 1.09e2, 3.36e2, 1.07e3, 3.44e3 at h = 0.24, 0.12, 0.06, 0.03 (ratios ~3.1-3.2 per halving, i.e. max w ~ h^-1.65). So h -> 0 is exactly the limit in which this frame's weights diverge as well; the extrapolation above is over a window in which max w grows by a factor 32, and a much finer h would eventually re-enter the regime where the T2 artefact mechanism (below) operates.
(2) SECONDARY FRAME, ARTEFACT-SUSPECT, S10 spectral circle model: the criterion FAILS at every L = 64, 96, 128, 192, 256, with lam_min(M_*)/||M_*|| = -0.206, -0.0075, -0.0352, -0.0579, -0.0498 and lam_min(M_* - tau_*) equal to it to 4 digits (f2_kkt_f1_L.out). That verdict must NOT be used, for three reasons, all in F1's normalisation as printed by f2_capscan.py (file f2_capscan_L128.out; the half-SLD convention of kkt_continuum.gQ_sld would halve lam_min and quarter the gain): (i) it is not cap-stable -- at L = 128, taper uv = 0.30, lam_min(M_*) = -3.211e-3, -3.134e-3, -7.887e-3, -3.477e-2, -1.050e-1 and lam_min/||M_*|| = -0.0122, -0.0067, -0.0105, -0.0352, -0.0753 for cap = 1e4, 1e6, 1e8, 1e10, 1e12, while theta is cap-stable to 5 digits (0.29117, 0.29119, 0.29116, 0.29118, 0.29119); (ii) the achievable gain collapses as the cap grows: rank-one gain/g_Q(dc) = 1.463e-4, 1.948e-6, 1.722e-10, 3.534e-11, 3.718e-12 on the same ladder (the violating directions have diverging curvature, g_Q(noise)/g_Q(dc) = 1.3e3 ... 5.5e13); the second taper uv = 0.20 repeats the pattern (lam_min/||M_*|| = -0.0125, -0.0070, -0.0088, -0.0258, -0.0287; gain = 5.808e-4 ... 6.444e-13) with theta shifted by 10% (0.2615); (iii) the mechanism: the circle model violates Moebius rigidity at O(1/L) (|dc_DD|/|dc| = 0.346, 0.214, 0.153, 0.101, 0.075 and |dc_AA|/|dc| = 0.048, 0.032, 0.024, 0.016, 0.012 at L = 64..256, both ~ 1/L, whereas the exact defect is purely A-D off-diagonal), and g_Q weights those spurious blocks by w up to the cap -- taken separately the blocks of delta_c carry g_Q of order 1e5 x g_Q(delta_c), so t_* and hence M_*, tau_* are contaminated exactly where the weights are largest.
WHAT MAY AND MAY NOT BE CONCLUDED. The numerics are consistent with the isometric orbit carrying the tangent optimum and kappa_opt = 1 - theta, and they exclude any O(1) gain from non-isometric or boundary-moving directions (every measured gain is <= 4e-4 g_Q(ddot) and falls like h^1.85/Ymax^2). They do NOT establish that the optimal N_1, Y_1 vanish: Thm 4.4(d) delivers a global minimiser, not uniqueness, and the marginal case lam_min -> 0^- found here is precisely where uniqueness is not delivered.

cards.title: KKT sign criterion: when the isometric orbit carries the all-channel second-order optimum
cards.statement: Let delta_* be the b-orthogonal residual of ddelta on the closure of the LINEAR class L = {[Q,G] : G bounded anti-self-adjoint, supported in D} (no minimiser is posited), t_* := SLD(delta_*) (S_Q(t_*) = delta_*, t_*~_ik = w_ik delta_*~_ik), tau_* := E_D t_* E_D and M_* := (1/2) E_D (t_* Q + Q t_*) E_D = Herm(t_{*,DA} Q_AD) + Herm(t_{*,DD} Q_DD) = Herm((t_* Q)_DD). Since w is unbounded, t_* need NOT be Hilbert-Schmidt: M_* and tau_* are quadratic FORMS, defined intrinsically by <psi,M_* psi> := 4 b(delta_*, A(0,|psi><psi|,0)) and <psi,tau_* psi> := -4 b(delta_*, A(0,0,|psi><psi|)) on the domain D of psi for which those directions lie in the form domain; 'M_* >= 0' is a form inequality and lambda_min may be -inf. Normalisation: g_Q(delta) = (1/4) Tr(t_delta delta), V(t_delta) = 2 g_Q(delta), d g_Q(delta)[eta] = (1/2) Tr(t_delta eta) (S10 (C4) is internally inconsistent with its own S_Q(t) = delta; the ratio and all sign conditions are unaffected). Derivative along an admissible non-isometric direction: (1/2)[Tr(N_1 M_*) - Tr(Y_1 tau_*)]. Conditions: (a) M_* >= 0 and M_* - tau_* >= 0; (c) Tr(N_1 M_*) >= Tr[(N_1^{1/2} tau_* N_1^{1/2})_+] for all bounded N_1 >= 0; (a) <=> (c), and (b) M_* >= (tau_*)_+ is sufficient but strictly stronger (the operator order is not a lattice). AMENDED after the referee report: (a) alone is NECESSARY but NOT SUFFICIENT. The feasible cone also contains the one-sided boundary-moving isometry directions (unbounded generators), which are not covered by (a), so global optimality of the isometric point is (a) AND (e), where (e) E(zeta) := 2 b(delta_*, A(zeta,0,0)) >= 0 for every admissible isometry generator zeta with A(zeta,0,0) in the form domain. E MUST be evaluated on the blocks of A (A_AD = -Q_AD zeta, A_DD = -(zeta* Q_DD + Q_DD zeta)): the commutator form -2 b(delta_*,[Q,zeta]) is valid only for BOUNDED anti-self-adjoint zeta (where E = 0) and is identically blind to the boundary form - F2 T5 finds it returns only the CG residual (-8e-6 ... -1e-2) even for zeta_inf, whose true value is 2 lambda (1-theta) g_Q(ddelta). E vanishes on the linear class and, when cyclicity Tr(t_*[Q,zeta]) = Tr([t_*,Q] zeta) is legitimate, E(zeta) = (1/2)Tr(E_D[Q,t_*]E_D zeta) = 0 by the stationarity Prop 4.3: E is exactly the cyclicity anomaly, i.e. a pure BOUNDARY functional, equal to (1/2)Tr((-2 sigma_zeta) M_*) on the boundary form of zeta. In the modular frame D = {y>0} has two endpoints and the cone is generated modulo the linear class by zeta_0 = -E_D d/dy E_D (the shift semigroup g(y) -> g(y-a), i.e. x -> 1 - e^{-a}(1-x); moves the junction y=0) and zeta_inf = -lambda D_chi|_D (further compression; moves y=+inf). PROVED: E(zeta_inf) = 2 lambda (1-theta) g_Q(ddelta) > 0. So, ON THE MODEL CONE, (e) reduces to the single inequality E(zeta_0) = 2 b(delta_*, A(zeta_0,0,0)) >= 0, with the identity (1/2) Tr((-2 sigma_{zeta_0}) M_*) valid only if -2 sigma_{zeta_0} lies in the form domain of M_* - which fails here (delta_0 (x) delta_0 is unbounded), so E(zeta_0) = +inf and (e) is vacuous at zeta_0 rather than satisfied with a margin. If (a) and (e) hold then kappa_opt = 1 - theta exactly (numerically 0.616 +- 0.003), modulo H1 and H2; if (a) fails with a gain bounded away from zero then kappa_opt < 1 - theta strictly, but a violating psi must have finite g_Q(d_psi) - a violation vanishing with the weight cap or the mesh is a regularisation artefact. HYPOTHESIS H3 (cone hypothesis, Def 4.12, read in the form domain F): for every admissible isometry generator zeta with A(zeta,0,0) in F there are alpha, beta >= 0 and eta in the b-closure of the linear class with A(zeta,0,0) = alpha A(zeta_0,0,0) + beta A(zeta_inf,0,0) + eta. (No boundary-form reformulation: that would be strictly weaker, trivially true for zeta = i m(y), and would not imply (e).) The reduction to the two model directions is PROVED ONLY for generators of vector-field type; multiplicity->1 shift semigroups (Cooper-Wold) and unbounded skew-adjoint zeta = i m(y) outside the closure of the linear class escape both arguments, and excluding them is exactly the content of H3. Since A(zeta_0,0,0) is NOT in F, the identity forces alpha = 0, so under H3 condition (e) holds OUTRIGHT via E(zeta_inf) > 0 and the junction inequality is never invoked; E(zeta_0) >= 0 remains the operative test for REGULARISED junction directions (finite mesh), which is what F2 T5 measures. Numerically (a) holds in the limit and E(zeta_0) > 0 on the model cone (F2 T4/T5, card kkt-noise-criterion-numerics) - with the caveat that the continuum piece is the CORNER term (~h^-0.60), not the tabulated total (~h^-0.97, dominated by a scheme-dependent upwind-viscosity term), and that both diverge, so A(zeta_0,0,0) is not in the form domain and (e) is vacuous rather than satisfied at zeta_0. Hence kappa_opt = 1 - theta = 0.616 +- 0.003 conditional on H1, H2 AND H3. Numerics (F2 T4, rigid frame of Prop 6.2): lambda_min(M_*)/||M_*|| = -4.1e-3, -1.9e-3, -8.2e-4, -3.7e-4 at h = 0.24, 0.12, 0.06, 0.03 (violation ~ h^1.15 and ~ 1/Ymax, rank-one gain ~ h^1.85), i.e. (a) holds for the exact problem. F2 T5 (endpoint): E(zeta_0)/g_Q(ddelta) = +34.1, +66.9, +131.3, +258.0 at h = 0.24, 0.12, 0.06, 0.03 for the admissible backward/dissipative scheme (centred = 0, the linear class; forward = inadmissible, negative), corner term (1/2) M_*(0,0)/h = +10.3 ... +37.2 growing like h^-0.6, so M_*(y,y) -> +inf as y -> 0+ and E(zeta_0) = +inf in the continuum: the junction direction is infinitely penalised at first order, consistent with M_* being a form; E(zeta_inf) reproduces 2(1-theta_h) g_Q to 1e-15, and the A-form and boundary-form expressions agree to 2e-10 ... 2e-8. Stationarity on the LINEAR class forces E_D[Q,t_*]E_D = 0, i.e. (t_* Q)_DD = M_* self-adjoint: S10's condition (S), which fails at the compression, holds automatically at the new point. Dictionary to S10 Thm 3.2: Sigma_2 -> (tQ)_DD is the loss-of-isometry (N_1) condition M >= 0; Sigma_1 = Sigma_2 - t_DD >= 0 is the NOISE (Y_1) condition M >= tau; Sigma_1 = Sigma_1* is the rotation condition.

cards.title: Second-order network law: Phi_tot = sum zeta_j zeta_k G(y_j - y_k), G = c Ghat universal
cards.statement: For corners at modular positions y_k with strengths zeta_k (frame of the whole chain), -log F(omega, omega o beta_Phi) = sum_{j,k} zeta_j zeta_k G(y_j - y_k) + o(|zeta|^2) with G(Delta) = c Ghat(Delta), Ghat(0) = 1/(12 pi^2) (Theorem A), Ghat even and positive-definite as the Fourier transform of the positive spectral density of the first-order corner defect in the modular frame (positive-definiteness does NOT imply Ghat >= 0 pointwise; the sign for Delta > 0 is open, card corner-correlation-kernel). The remainder must be shown UNIFORM in the corner separations for the applications in which zeta -> 0 and Delta -> inf together (vwz-protocol-ordering). Lower bound: data processing + Legendre form, linear in the defect. Upper bound: Uhlmann + C^{1,1} flow extension with finitely many second-derivative jumps; expected global bound Phi_tot <= -(1/2) log(1 - 2 sum zeta zeta G). Separation constraint: admissible protocols ALL of whose corners are weak (zeta_j <= eps for every j) cannot have two of them close at distinct points -- for the L->R Petz chain (e^{Delta_k} - 1) zeta_k^(I) = 2 r_k (1+v_k)/(1+r_k) >= 2 r_k/(1+r_k) exactly, and zeta_j <= eps for all j forces e^{Delta_k} >= 2/eps, PROVED in rigor/network_corner_calculus.tex Thm 11.1 (track G1a; REF-P6-3: stands; sharp as eps -> 0, exact minima 20.0499, 66.6817, 200.0050, 666.6682 at eps = 0.1, 0.03, 0.01, 0.003, rigor/ref_p6_3_separation.out; 1/eps for general admissible s_k >= lambda_k; card corner-separation-constraint); with only the pair weak the separation can stay O(1). Hence, for all-weak L->R chains and given the uniform remainder, at strict second order Phi_tot = f2 sum_points (sum_steps zeta)^2 + O(eps^2 sup_{Delta >= log(2/eps)} |Ghat(Delta)|): coherent addition at a common junction, additivity in zeta^2 across distinct junctions. cards.title: Corner data of all one-sided protocols for n = 4 and n = 5: the holonomy is the starting block
cards.statement: For a complete one-sided protocol with SINGLE-interval conditioning, starting block J_0 = A_i..A_j (j >= i+1) and common rotation parameter t (theta_t = (1+e^{-2 pi t})/2, theta_0 = 1 the ordinary Petz value), hypothesis (H) holds and the corner measure is kappa = sum_{k<i} sigma^L_k delta_{p_{k+2}} + sum_{k>j} sigma^R_k delta_{p_{k-1}} with sigma^L_k = theta_t 2 l_k/(l_{k+1}(l_k+l_{k+1})) and sigma^R_k = theta_t 2 l_k/(l_{k-1}(l_{k-1}+l_k)) -- INDEPENDENT of the order of the steps. Hence all binom((i-1)+(n-j), i-1) orders for a given starting block give the same recovered state, the 2^{n-2} protocols with a starting PAIR fall into exactly n-1 classes (one per pair), the left corners occupy p_3..p_{i+1} and the right corners p_j..p_{n-1}, and they overlap in exactly one point (a double corner at p_{i+1} = p_j) iff j = i+1. n = 4 (4 protocols, 3 classes): start A_1A_2 (RR) -> {p_2: sigma^R_3, p_3: sigma^R_4} = VWZ Protocol 2; start A_2A_3 (LR and RL, identical) -> {p_3: sigma^L_1 + sigma^R_4} = VWZ Protocol 3; start A_3A_4 (LL) -> {p_3: sigma^L_1, p_4: sigma^L_2}. Equal lengths l = (1,1,1,1): zeta^(I) = (0.75 at p_2, 1 at p_3), (2 at p_3), (1 at p_3, 0.75 at p_4). n = 5 (8 protocols, 4 classes): start A_1A_2 (RRR) -> p_2,p_3,p_4 simple; start A_2A_3 (LRR, RLR, RRL) -> double corner at p_3 plus p_4; start A_3A_4 (LLR, LRL, RLL) -> p_3 plus double corner at p_4; start A_4A_5 (LLL) -> p_3,p_4,p_5 simple. Union-conditioning variants for n = 4: VWZ 1(A) (one corner at p_2) and 1(B) (two corners at p_2, same measure by the identity 2c/(b(b+c)) + 2d/((b+c)(b+c+d)) = 2(c+d)/(b(b+c+d))) satisfy (H); the variant 'add D on C, then A on BC' does NOT (REF-P6-0's counterexample geometry: the mass is displaced off the junction).
cards.verify: rigor/g1a_calculus.py section 5 enumerates all protocols for n = 4, 5, checks that they fall into n-1 classes, and measures every Schwarzian mass of the composite map by one-sided finite differences (agreement to 3e-3 relative).

Three deliverables sharing one folder: (A) a README of about 250 lines replacing the current 80, with eight figures, four of which already exist (collapse, gap_decay, thermal_shield, cfun_flow) and four generated as SVG by tools/make_figures.py (geometry schematic; Phi against zeta over the measured range 0.0083-17.07 with the asymptote and remainder; the coefficient across models, all measured at c = 1 with the c-linearity drawn as Theorem B rather than as data; the theta convergence ladder; the corner calculus); (B) an interactive site served from docs/ on GitHub Pages with .nojekyll, plain ES modules, vendored KaTeX, no runtime external requests, ten modules; (C) a generated documentation set docs/{index,status,notation,definitions,open,sources,history}.md plus docs/results/<id>.md, produced from the knowledge base by tools/build_docs.py with a make check that fails on drift. COVERAGE: the consequential set is the 33 refereed-or-proved claims (30 proved, 3 refereed) plus the 11 headline numericals the modules display, 44 of the 81 cards; the module table names every claim each module carries, and module 10 reaches the rest. HONESTY RULES: badges are per displayed claim and not per module, a conditional badge names its hypotheses (all-channel-optimum-value under H1-H3, the junction form of the corner calculus under H), numerical is never styled like proved, and a card that has never been refereed is not displayed at all, which makes a referee pass on circle-model-taper-suppresses-theta a prerequisite for module 5. Module 6 must implement the UNCONDITIONAL Theorem 5.2 of network_corner_calculus.tex (masses at the preimages of the junctions, scaled by the later maps derivatives) and present the junction form of Theorem 5.3 as the special case under (H), flagging configurations where (H) fails, because implementing only the junction form would teach a false theorem: (H) fails for single-interval starts and for union conditioning, and there the naive corner measure is wrong; the Protocol 3 panel must state that its map equals the over-compressed Theorem-A map only up to post-composition with a global Moebius map. Every displayed number ships as a JSON record {value, error, source, line, status} whose source is a repository path, and make check fails on drift. Other constraints: no third-party excerpt on the public surface; PDFs are gitignored build products; free-tier Pages serves public repositories only; the browser cannot redo ball arithmetic, SDPs or Galerkin solves; CI is red until implementation_C11.tex and its referee report build. Also planned: CITATION.cff and a Zenodo DOI, a .github issue template, deletion or marking of the frozen plan_page/petz_program_plan.html, and a 3 MB budget for site assets. Five phases with a referee pass each, 4-6 agent-days, an estimated 4M-6M tokens, with a stated reduction to two modules if that is too much. Four decisions open: D1 when Pages goes live, D2 how readers get the PDFs (option (c) also needs an exception to the *.pdf ignore rule), D3 how many modules, D4 whether the site carries the AI provenance (recommended yes, in the papers wording).

cards.title: Exact root fidelity of two quasi-free CAR states from their symbols (Note 5 Thm. 2.1)
cards.statement: For two gauge-invariant quasi-free states on a FINITE-DIMENSIONAL one-particle space h with symbols Q1, Q2 (0 < Q < 1), G = Q/(1-Q): -log F = (1/2) sum log(1+t) + (1/2) sum log(1+s) - sum log(1 + sqrt(tau)), t = eig G1, s = eig G2, tau = eig(G1^{1/2} G2 G1^{1/2}) (Note 5 Thm. 2.1, thm:finite-fidelity); equivalently F = det(1-Q1)^{1/2} det(1-Q2)^{1/2} prod_i (1 + sigma_i(C)), C = (1-Q1)^{-1/2} Q1^{1/2} Q2^{1/2} (1-Q2)^{-1/2}, the form that is numerically stable when eigenvalues sit near 0 and 1. For infinite-dimensional h the formula is obtained as the monotone limit over finite-dimensional compressions (Note 5, Thm det-rep) when the two states are quasi-equivalent. Implemented in mpmath at dps 60-80 and validated against the brute-force many-body fidelity on three random modes to 12 digits.
cards.verify: Note 5 Thm. 2.1; numerics/optimality/petz_ref.py (mpmath, 60-90 digits); selftest() in numerics/optimality_all/exact_fidelity_rotated.py.

cards.title: Second-order problem over quasi-free channels is a convex SDP
cards.statement: Gauge-invariant quasi-free channels have data (X,Y), CP iff Y >= 0 and XX* + Y <= 1; in the variables (X, Z = X Q_BB X* + Y) the feasible set F = {X Q_BB X* <= Z <= 1 - X(1-Q_BB)X*} is convex and semidefinite representable, the recovered symbol is affine, and the SLD form g_Q is a convex quadratic; every local minimum is global. Caveat: g_Q is the second-order term only for defects small relative to e^{-kappa_max} (order of limits); cap weights, never drop modes.

cards.title: Two git repositories over one work tree: public project, private third-party material
cards.statement: Since 2026-09-20 the cft_cmi directory is covered by two git repositories sharing one work tree, so no file moved and no tool was reconfigured. .git holds the publishable project (406 files, 5.9 MB: papers, notes, rigor documents, numerics scripts and the 97 result captures the KB cites as evidence), remote https://github.com/alexander-stottmeister/cft-cmi; .git-private holds what must not be published (229 files, 47.7 MB: the 178 page excerpts in rigor/shots, the 47 source PDFs in refs, CHECKLIST.md, PRIVATE.md, pgit, pgit-exclude), remote https://github.com/alexander-stottmeister/cft-cmi-private, driven by the wrapper ./pgit (status, sync, check, push). BOTH REMOTES ARE PRIVATE as of 2026-09-20; the first is public-ready but not public. The two tracked sets are disjoint (overlap 0) and the files tracked by neither are regenerable build products and caches (196 MB). Three things make it work: (1) rigor_preamble.tex defines \\shot[width]{file} and \\shotc, an exact drop-in for \\includegraphics that embeds the excerpt when rigor/shots is present and prints a framed locator note when absent -- 255 call sites in 19 documents were converted, local builds are unchanged (network_corner_calculus 42 pp with images) and a clone of the REMOTE builds with one placeholder per call site (quadratic_limit 26 pp / 0 images against 27 pp / 8 locally, verified by REF-INFRA-2); (2) the 24 python scripts that hardcoded /Users/alex now resolve paths against a computed _ROOT (37 literals), and the four shell scripts that hardcoded a session scratchpad interpreter now honour $PYTHON; (3) because a work-tree .gitignore outranks info/exclude, the private repo cannot see NEW files under its own paths, so ./pgit sync force-stages them and ./pgit check fails on either an overlap or untracked excerpts; since a bare clone carries no info/exclude, the whitelist is tracked as pgit-exclude and ./pgit reinstalls it on every run. The public history never contained an excerpt or a source PDF (verified against a clone of the remote), so making it public later needs no history rewrite. Licensing: MIT for code, CC BY 4.0 for documents and data, no third-party material redistributed (THIRD-PARTY.md). KNOWLEDGE BASE: unaffected, and it is a third repository (claude-team-kb, ../kb) with its own sync. Every evidence pointer resolves on a machine carrying all three clones, and none fails. EIGHT targets live in the private repo and are cited by EIGHT cards (counting doc:, num:, ref: tokens in areas/, claims/ and evidence/, excluding the generated INDEX, SUMMARY and CHANGELOG): six source papers (AlbertiUhlmann02_math-ph-0202038, BJL_twisted_duality_math-ph-0204029, CDIT_1808.02384, Sion1958_minimax, Uhlmann76, VWZ_2307.14434) plus doc:CHECKLIST.md and doc:PRIVATE.md. A machine with only the public clone loses those pointers, and refs/restore.sh is not a substitute: of the six papers it recovers exactly ONE under the cited filename (VWZ); Uhlmann76 is tabled as paywalled, CDIT is tabled as CDIW21 so restoring writes a different filename, and the remaining three (AlbertiUhlmann02, BJL_twisted_duality, Sion1958_minimax) appear in REFERENCES.md only as bullet entries, not as rows of the table restore.sh parses. The review packets the KB writes into rigor/ are tracked by neither repository. A new machine needs three clones as siblings: kb, cft_cmi, and cft-cmi-private into cft_cmi/.git-private, with the fetch refspec, upstream and ./pgit check that PRIVATE.md spells out (recipe verified end to end by REF-INFRA-2b: shots and refs restored, status clean, document builds with images).

cards.title: Type-III sequential recovery bound: Bures angles add along a chain of von Neumann inclusions
cards.statement: Let omega be a normal state on a von Neumann algebra M, N_1 subset N_2 subset ... subset N_m subset M von Neumann subalgebras with the same unit, and R_k: N_{k+1} -> N_k normal unital 2-positive (Heisenberg-picture) recovery maps, R = R_1 o ... o R_{m-1}. TWO FORMS. (a) ANGLE FORM (Thm 12.5), under hypothesis (U): with the Bures angle A(phi,psi) = arccos F(phi,psi), A(omega|N_m, omega|N_1 o R) <= sum_k A(omega|N_{k+1}, omega|N_k o R_k). (b) CHORDAL FORM (Thm 12.6), UNCONDITIONAL: the same telescoping for the Bures distance d_B = sqrt(2 - 2F), whose triangle inequality is Alberti-Uhlmann 2002 Prop. 1(1), p. 3 (on disk; stated there WITHOUT proof and attributed to Bures 1969, which is NOT OBTAINED). Both proofs telescope through mu_j = omega|N_{m-j} o R_{m-j} o S_j with S_j = R_{m-j+1} o ... o R_{m-1} and use monotonicity of F under the channel S_j. Ingredients proved in the document: the Choi inequality T(a^{-1}) >= T(a)^{-1} for unital 2-positive T (Schur complement), monotonicity of F from Alberti-Uhlmann 2002 Thm 2(1), p. 6 (product form) and Cor 2(5), p. 8 (normalised form) plus eq. (1-4), and the spherical triangle inequality <x,z> >= cos(alpha+beta). HYPOTHESIS (U), declared, NOT dischargeable: in the standard form of a sigma-finite von Neumann algebra, F(phi,psi) = <xi_phi, xi_psi> for the natural-cone representatives. Sources: Araki-Raggio 1982 is NOT OBTAINED (not in refs/); Uhlmann 1976 IS on disk (refs/Uhlmann76.pdf) and was read -- it contains the explicit-formula theorem (p. 277), one-argument concavity of the transition probability (eq. (8), p. 274) and monotonicity under RESTRICTION to a subalgebra (eq. (24), p. 277), but no standard-form/natural-cone statement, no CP-monotonicity and no metric statement, so (U) cannot be cited from it (the earlier claim that both sources were NOT OBTAINED was factually wrong). (U) is used ONLY for the angle form (a) and for the exact form Phi_tot <= -log cos(sum_k arccos e^{-Phi_k}). SECOND-ORDER FORM (Cor 12.7), UNCONDITIONAL: Phi_tot <= (sum_k sqrt(Phi_k))^2 (1+o(1)) as all Phi_k -> 0, obtained from the chordal form (b) via d_B = sqrt(2 Phi)(1+O(Phi)); if each step extends to a normal unital 2-positive map on F(I) with error Phi_k^(I) then Phi_k <= Phi_k^(I) and the same bound holds with Phi_k^(I). SATURATION at second order iff all corners coincide (then Phi_tot = Phi_A(sum zeta_k) = f2 (sum zeta_k)^2 = (sum sqrt(Phi_k))^2); for distinct corners the bound is far from sharp, the network law W2 replacing (sum zeta)^2 by sum_{jk} zeta_j zeta_k Ghat(y_j-y_k)/Ghat(0).
cards.verify: No numerics needed: the proof is from the cited variational formula plus elementary Hilbert-space geometry. The saturation statement uses Theorem A (card thm-a-quadratic-law) and the Protocol 3 reduction (corner-calculus).

cards.title: Exact (N,Y,V) chart of F and the tangent problem at the compression
cards.statement: Feasible set: (X,Z) in F iff N := 1 - X X* >= 0 and Y := Z - X Q_BB X* satisfies 0 <= Y <= N. Polar: X = (1-N)^{1/2} V with V : h_B -> h_D the polar partial isometry; V V* = 1 - 1_{{1}}(N), so the POLAR V is a co-isometry iff 1 is not an eigenvalue of N (sharp: for X = the forward shift no co-isometric factor exists); existence of SOME co-isometric factor is the weaker dim ker(1-N) <= dim ker X. Then V* = W U with W the compression unitary h_D -> h_B and U an isometry of h_D (onto iff V unitary). Scaling N = s N_1 (N_1 a bounded positive operator), Y = s Y_1, U_s = 1 + s zeta + o(s) with (U_s) a C_0-semigroup of isometries gives, exactly feasible at every small s, the first-order defect (as sesquilinear forms on C_c^inf) delta^(1) = ddelta + A(zeta,N_1,Y_1) with A_AA = 0, A_AD = -Q_AD zeta + (1/2) Q_AD N_1, A_DD = -(zeta* Q_DD + Q_DD zeta) + (1/2){N_1,Q_DD} - Y_1 (noise enters DD with a MINUS sign); ddelta = [Q,d] with d = E_I D_chi E_I (Lemma 6.1), and ddelta has zero AA block (locality of D_chi, chi = chi' = 0 on A) and zero DD block (Moebius rigidity, S10 Lemma 11.1). Boundary-moving (non-surjective) isometry directions: the absorption identity A(zeta,N_1,Y_1) = A(G, N_1 - 2 sigma, Y_1) holds with G = anti-symmetric part and sigma <= 0 the BOUNDARY FORM <sigma g,g> := Re<zeta* g,g> on dom(zeta*) (sigma <= 0 by Lumer-Phillips for the adjoint contraction semigroup; for BOUNDED zeta, sigma = 0 and zeta is anti-self-adjoint, so bounded isometry families give nothing beyond S10's class). This yields only an INCLUSION of cones: the anti-symmetric G on the right must themselves be isometry generators. The inclusion cannot be reversed - +lambda D_chi|_D is anti-symmetric but generates an OUTWARD flow, and admitting it would give delta^(1) = (1-lambda) ddelta and tangent value T = 0. Also the singular boundary N_1 are NOT in the g_Q-closure of the bounded ones (||Q_AD N_1^(n)||_2 -> inf), so they need their own one-sided condition, not a limit. The tangent value T = inf g_Q(delta^(1)) is an upper bound for limsup z^{-2} min_F g_Q under hypothesis H1 (g_Q-differentiability along the scaled family); the matching lower bound needs hypothesis H2 (Def 3.16: a minimiser EXISTS, is of the scaled-family form, with ||N_1||+||Y_1|| <= C and a uniform o(s^2) remainder - i.e. H2 is the lower bound in disguise), which is NOT proved: g_Q >= (1/4)||.||_2^2 gives O(s) defect blocks but does not localise (X,Z) because Q_AB has 0 in its essential spectrum.

cards.title: Tangent SDP over (G, N1, Y1) in the circle model: orbit-only optimum matches (1-theta) to 1.1e-7, full optimum not resolvable (measured Gram cond 2.4e22)
cards.statement:
The fixed-geometry tangent problem, min over G = iH anti-Hermitian on D, N1 >= 0, 0 <= Y1 <= N1 of g_Q(delta_c + [G,Q] + noise(N1,Y1)) with noise_DD = (1/2){N1,Q_DD} - Y1, noise_DA = (1/2) N1 Q_DA, noise_AA = 0, was posed as an SDP in the S10 spectral circle model (cvxpy, CLARABEL/SCS). SOLID OUTPUTS. (a) The ORBIT-ONLY restriction (N1 = Y1 = 0 forced) reproduces (1 - theta) g_Q(delta_c) to 1.1e-7 relative at L = 64 (cap 1e10) and 4.0e-7 (cap 1e6) -- this is agreement to 1.1e-7, not "exactly", and it is a statement about the orbit-only problem, i.e. a validation of the SDP formulation against the S10 CG, not about the full tangent optimum. (b) Homogeneity: delta_c -> 2 delta_c scales the ORBIT-ONLY optimum by exactly 4.00000000 in both the direct and the Gram form (L = 64, cap 1e6). (c) The rank-one gains along the KKT-violating directions, computed exactly without a solver, are 6.3e-9, 1.8e-12, 3.5e-11, 1.2e-10, 1.1e-10 in units of g_Q(delta_c) at L = 64, 96, 128, 192, 256 (cap 1e10), and the isometric rotations cannot absorb those directions (g_red/g_Q = 1 - 5e-4); no statement about kappa_opt is made here (that is the business of card kkt-noise-criterion-numerics, in a frame where rigidity is exact). (d) Subspace lower bounds on the gain (f2_sub_gain_fixed.out; each returned (N1,Y1) is checked for cone feasibility, and l and g_red are recomputed exactly outside the solver, so the numbers are valid lower bounds independently of the solver's own objective): at L = 64, subspace eigMtau k=4 gives gain/g_Q(delta_c) = 2.843e-07 (status optimal, cone feasibility -2.4e-12), svdQDA k=4 gives 9.204e-09 (optimal_inaccurate, -4.4e-14), mix k=8 gives 2.106e-04 (optimal_inaccurate, cone feasibility -3.4e-17, l recomputed -1.0000, g_red recomputed 3.2049e+05 by CG; the solver's own objective 6.970e+05 is 2.17x higher, i.e. the returned point is better than the solver thought, and a non-converged CG would only weaken the bound); at L = 128, eigMtau k=4 gives 5.586e-10 (optimal_inaccurate, -7.8e-16). Hence kappa_full <= 1 - theta - 2.106e-4 = 0.64883481 at L = 64 (1 - theta = 0.64904541) and kappa_full <= 0.70882131 at L = 128 (1 - theta = 0.70882131 to 9 digits). The remaining subspaces return no point, with honest solver statuses: infeasible_inaccurate (eigM and rand at L = 64, eigM and mix at L = 128) and infeasible (svdQDA at L = 128).
CORRECTION TO THE FIRST VERSION OF THIS CARD. The earlier statement "at L = 128 and 256 every subspace solve failed" was wrong in its cause: the script crashed with "ValueError: matmul: Input operand 1 does not have enough dimensions" whenever the solver returned no point, because of an unguarded basis @ Nr.value with Nr.value = None. That is a code defect, not conditioning. It has been fixed (status caught, SCS fallback, cone feasibility measured) and the run redone; the table above is the corrected result.
WHAT IS NOT RESOLVED: the FULL tangent optimum kappa_full in the circle model. The quadratic form is numerically singular there: measured Gram condition numbers (f2_gram_cond.out, 3|D|^2 real coordinates) are 2.50e+18 (L = 64, cap 1e4), 2.65e+19 (L = 64, cap 1e6), 2.37e+22 (L = 64, cap 1e10) and 2.51e+26 (L = 96, cap 1e10), with the smallest positive eigenvalue at the double-precision floor -- a direct consequence of the circle model's O(1/L) violation of Moebius rigidity, since the individual blocks of delta_c carry g_Q of order 1e5 x g_Q(delta_c). Consequences observed: CLARABEL fails with SolverError on the direct form at L = 64 for caps 1e4 and 1e10 and on the scale-free cone form for all caps; SCS does not converge in 1e5 iterations; the Gram-reduced form appears to succeed but its answer is a rank-cutoff artefact (it drops 161 of 675 directions below tol*max and then reports kappa_full = 0.5990 against 1 - theta = 0.6490 at L = 64, a spurious 5 percent gain obtained by treating small-curvature directions as free); and the UNCONSTRAINED relaxation (arbitrary Hermitian N1, Y1, no cone) is genuinely ill-posed -- CG on Ghat x = l does not converge and the gain estimate grows monotonically with the iteration count (8.7e-4 -> 6.8e-3 of g_Q(delta_c) between iterations 75 and 200 at L = 64), because with Y1 free the DD block of the defect can be set arbitrarily. The cone constraints are therefore essential and the correct scale-free formulation is q* = min{g_Q([G,Q] + noise(v)) : l(v) = -1, v in the cone} with gain = 1/(4 q*), l(v) = Tr(N1 M_*) - Tr(Y1 tau_*) in the half-SLD normalisation of t_*.
This card reports BOUNDS in the circle model, not a value, and in a frame whose criterion verdict is shown to be artefact-dominated (card kkt-noise-criterion-numerics).

cards.title: theta as a geometry-free Wiener-Hopf constant in the modular frame of I
cards.statement: Frame-free form: ddelta = [Q,d] with d = E_I D_chi E_I, and on the isometric orbit delta^(1) = [Q, d - zeta], so 1 - theta = inf_G g_Q([Q, d + G]) / g_Q([Q,d]), the INFIMUM over BOUNDED anti-self-adjoint G supported in D (not a min; the distinction from theta_HS is open, cf. exact_fidelity_upper_half.tex Rem 7.4(i)). In the modular frame of the half-line I = (-inf,1) — coordinate y = -log(1-x), implemented by the half-density push-forward, A = {y<0}, D = {y>0} — Bisognano-Wichmann makes Q a Fourier multiplier Q = (1 + e^{-2 pi p})^{-1}, p = -i d/dy, E_D = 1_{y>0}, and the compression field becomes w(y) = -4 sinh^2(y/2) 1_{y>0} (C^{1,1} at 0, ~ -e^y as y -> +inf: the moving endpoint x=1 sits at y=+inf). With X^ the kernel in the Fourier variable, g_Q([Q,X]) = (1/4) int int K(p,p') |X^(p,p')|^2, K(p,p') = sinh^2(pi(p-p')) / [cosh(pi(p-p')) (cosh(pi(p+p')) + cosh(pi(p-p')))]. So theta is the value of a parameter-free quadratic Wiener-Hopf problem (minimise over kernels supported in the quadrant y,y' > 0): theta is a pure number, independent of a,b,c,L,z. NUMERICAL VALUE (track F3, numerics/optimality_all/F3_RESULTS.md, f3_t0.py): theta = 0.384 +- 0.003, 1 - theta = 0.616 +- 0.003; the modular Galerkin frame and a direct discretisation of the frame above agree to 3e-4 after extrapolation (order h^0.77, five mesh families), the modular window Lambda is irrelevant, and the residual h-dependence is a BULK effect (the endpoint piece saturates at coarse h). S10's 0.300 +- 0.005 is not a competing estimate but a TAPER-SUPPRESSED LOWER BOUND: relaxing the circle model's smoothstep UV taper moves theta at L=256 from 0.2896 to 0.36 and beyond. Consequently the three circulated candidates are EXCLUDED: 3/pi^2 = 0.30396 and 1/3 far below, 1 - 2/pi = 0.36338 still 6.9 sigma low; that all three fell in the old 0.30-0.40 window is a cautionary datum about unmotivated candidates. Structural reading: theta > 0 iff E_D u E_D != 0 (S10 Thm 6.2 + Cor 11.2, non-vanishing numerical). theta < 1 is NOT proved: only the converse is established (if d were anti-self-adjoint then G = -d would be admissible and theta = 1); d is skew-symmetric but not skew-adjoint, its boundary form sitting at the moving endpoint. K -> 1 as |p-p'| -> inf at fixed p+p', and K -> 0 as |p+p'| -> inf at fixed p-p' — the latter is the direction the circle taper suppresses, consistent with its downward bias. NO closed form is claimed or fitted.

cards.title: The first-order gain constant theta = 0.384 +- 0.003 (S10's 0.300 is a taper-suppressed lower bound)
cards.statement: theta = sup_G cos^2(u,v_G) = 0.384 +- 0.003, hence 1-theta = 0.616 +- 0.003. The two published values are reconciled: they are the SAME number at different resolutions, not different limits. Five independent discretisations of F1's geometry-free Wiener-Hopf problem (Prop 6.2) extrapolate to 0.3835-0.3847: T0 uniform cells in the modular coordinate y=-log(1-x) with y_max=10 (theta = 0.31367, 0.34236, 0.35934, 0.36945, 0.37544 at h = 0.24, 0.12, 0.06, 0.03, 0.015) and with y_max=20 (0.31581, 0.34395, 0.36036, 0.37009, 0.37380 at h = 0.24, 0.12, 0.06, 0.03, 0.02); the S11 modular Galerkin frame at a=1, L=2 with Lambda=12 (0.29797 ... 0.36644 at h = 0.32 ... 0.04) and Lambda=8 (0.36608, 0.36962, 0.37346 at h = 0.04, 0.03, 0.02); and the same Galerkin functional on the circle model's own mesh (0.34058, 0.35830, 0.36904, 0.37534, 0.37893 at L = 128...2048). The measured convergence order is h^0.77 +- 0.02 (successive-increment ratio rho = 0.577...0.592 per family -- A: 0.581-0.591, B: 0.581, 0.591, C: 0.577, 0.588, C': 0.592, D: 0.570-0.606 -- stable over four octaves down to h=0.015; fractional because the defect kernel -(i/2pi) sinh(y1/2) sinh(y2/2)/sinh^2((y1-y2)/2) is homogeneous of degree 0 at the corner y=0, confirmed by corner-graded meshes which saturate). The modular-window systematic obeys theta(y_max) = theta_inf - c(h)/y_max with c ~ h^0.6 (residual 1.5e-5), worth +0.0009 to +0.0032. theta is geometry independent: the spread is 5.1e-4 over the four Galerkin rows (a,L) = (1,2), (2,1), (1,4) and s = 0.1, 0.3 at fixed h=0.1, Lambda=12 (0.34843, 0.34894, 0.34854, 0.34863), and 2.0e-3 over the whole table once the T0 (inf,1) row is included (0.34695 at h=0.1, Y=Ymax=8) -- that extra spread is the frame change (T0's smaller modular window, worth about -1.5e-3 by the y_max law above), not the geometry, as Moebius covariance requires. S10 Sec 7(c)'s 0.300 +- 0.005 is a LOWER BOUND: its ultraviolet taper removes the modes carrying ~20% of theta (see finding circle-model-taper-suppresses-theta), and its 1/L Richardson uses the wrong variable (theta_circ rises linearly in log L: 0.28958 -> 0.30173 from L=256 to 1024 with no saturation). cards.title: (UH) proved: optimised Uhlmann bound = g_Q of the defect, for every isometric quasi-free channel
cards.statement: For an isometric quasi-free channel with one-particle isometry W_I, every unitary W~ of L^2(R) with W~|_{L^2(I)} = W_I and P^perp W~ P Hilbert-Schmidt gives -log F <= -1/2 log det(1 - V^*V) <= -1/2 log(1 - ||V||_2^2), V = P^perp W~ P (Prop. 1.3). The admissible extensions form a right torsor under {1_I (+) W'}: the whole column Z E_I is prescribed by the channel and the free block is E_{I^c} Z E_{I^c}, at first order / as an exact right translation (Lemma 4.1 -- NOT a block-diagonal Z_I (+) Z_e, and NOT the truncation E_I D_chi E_I). Reduction (Thm 4.3): inf over exterior Z_e of (1/2)||P^perp(Z_0+Z_e)P||^2 = (1/2) dist(P^perp Z_0 P, Ext)^2 = (1/2)||Pi P^perp Z_0 P||^2 + (1/2) dist((1-Pi)P^perp Z_0 P, Ext)^2 = g_Q(E_I[P,Z_0]E_I), the last step because closure(Ext) = N^perp always. Hence (UH) in its PROVED, g_Q-free form (Thm 7.1, eq. (18)): for the product family U_s = W~_s e^{-lambda s G} e^{s Z_e}, limsup_{s->0} s^{-2}(-log F(omega, omega^{beta_s})) <= (1/2) dist(P^perp(D_chi + lambda G)P, Ext)^2 = (1/2)||Pi P^perp (D_chi + lambda G) P||^2. Ingredients: the exact one-parameter-group estimate ||P^perp e^{tZ}P||_2 <= |t| ||P^perp Z P||_2 (Lemma 6.1) and an S_2-continuity argument for the three-factor product family (Thm 6.2); the limsup is taken at fixed Z_e and only then the infimum over Z_e (no uniformity in Z_e is claimed or needed). cards.title: Vacuum rigidity: the pulled-back vacuum is the vacuum iff the map is Moebius; no protocol recovers exactly
cards.statement: (a) ELEMENTARY RIGIDITY (Lem 7.1): if Phi: J -> R is C^1 with Phi' > 0 and sqrt(Phi'(x)Phi'(y))/(Phi(x)-Phi(y)) = 1/(x-y) for all x != y in J, then Phi is the restriction of a global Moebius map. Proof: the relation with y = y_1 fixed is the separable ODE g' = g^2/(c (x-y_1)^2) for g = Phi - Phi(y_1), c = Phi'(y_1), whose exact integral (1/g)' = (1/(c(x-y_1)))' gives Phi = Phi(y_1) + c(x-y_1)/(1 + A c (x-y_1)) on each side of y_1; varying the base point and using that two Moebius maps agreeing on an open interval are equal shows the two sides agree. (b) STATE RIGIDITY (Thm 7.3): for the chiral free fermion with vacuum kernel Q(x,y) = (1/2 pi i)(x-y-i0)^{-1}, the state omega o beta_{V_Phi} on F(I) equals the vacuum iff Phi is Moebius iff S(Phi) = 0; the 'only if' follows by testing the two-point function with disjointly supported functions (which avoids the diagonal) and applying (a), the 'if' from [V_g, P] = 0 for g in Moeb (the Moebius group preserves the Hardy space). (c) NO EXACT RECOVERY (Thm 7.3(2,3)): for EVERY non-empty one-sided protocol whose last step keeps a non-empty part, S(Phi) is a non-zero negative measure -- all masses in the general rule -2 sum_m sigma_m G_m'(x_m) delta_{x_m} have the same sign, so they cannot cancel, and the last step's mass is never displaced or swallowed (G_N = id). Hence omega o beta_P != omega and Phi_fid = -log F > 0, using that F = 1 forces equality of the states (Lem 7.2, proved from Alberti's inequality P_tr <= phi(a) psi(a^{-1}) with a = 1 + tb). This needs neither hypothesis (H) nor the second-order law. Degenerate exception: a step conditioning on the ENTIRE block has its corner at an endpoint of I, where beta_I = 0 and zeta = 0; such a step is a pure Moebius compression (Theorem A at a = 0) and is not a recovery in the Petz sense.

cards.title: VWZ four-interval protocols: Phi(1):Phi(2):Phi(3) -> 1:2:4; middle-out is the worst order
cards.statement: In Vardhan-Wei-Zou's symmetric setup (L_A = L_D = a, L_B = L_C = b, their eta (5.9) = a/(a+2b)), the corner calculus (card corner-calculus, open) gives exactly: single step (Protocol 1(A) = 1(B)) one corner of strength zeta_1 = a/b; L->R Protocol 2 corners zeta_2 = a(a+2b)/(2b(a+b)) at p_2 and zeta_3 = a/b at p_3 with e^{Delta_23} = 1/eta; Protocol 3 one double corner of strength 2a/b at p_3 (all checked by REF-P6-0). Hence, given the corner calculus, -log F^(1) : -log F^(3) = Phi_A(a/b) : Phi_A(2a/b) exactly for all eta (-> 1 : 4 as eta -> 0, Theorem A twice, no hypothesis on Ghat), and, CONDITIONAL on the second-order network law with a remainder uniform in the corner separation and on Ghat(Delta) -> 0 as Delta -> inf (both open, corner-correlation-kernel), -log F^(2) -> 2 x -log F^(1); exactly at second order Phi^(2)/Phi^(1) = (zeta_2^2 + zeta_3^2)/zeta_1^2 + (2 zeta_2 zeta_3/zeta_1^2) Ghat(log 1/eta)/Ghat(0). Middle-out is the worst of the three orders at second order with no sign hypothesis: by Cauchy-Schwarz Phi^(2) <= f2 (zeta_2 + zeta_3)^2 < f2 (2 zeta_1)^2 = Phi^(3) because zeta_2 < zeta_1. VWZ (5.10)-(5.11), Fig. 25 state: "-log F^(2) ~ -log F^(3) ∝ f' c eta^2 with f' < f, confirming that the sequential recovery is less effective than the single-step case" -- their inequality and their prose point opposite ways; the calculus contradicts the inequality (f'_3 = 4f exactly) and, at small eta, the approximate equality of Protocols 2 and 3. Their single-step coefficient (2.13), f2 ~ 0.070 c, matches our ordinary-Petz prediction 8 f2 = 0.0675 c (zeta = 2z). Fig. 25 CANNOT be read as a measurement of Ghat (REF-P6-1, rigor/ref_p6_1_fig25.py): Delta_23 = log(1/eta) is bounded below by their axis (eta^2 <= 0.4 gives Delta_23 >= 0.46), the corner strengths there are O(1) (zeta_1 = 2 eta/(1-eta) >= 0.22 for eta >= 0.1) so the second-order law does not apply, and Phi^(2) = Phi^(3) at second order would need Ghat(Delta_23)/Ghat(0) = 1.1 ... 2.1 > 1, which positive-definiteness forbids; no value or sign of Ghat can be extracted from their figure -- G3 measures Ghat directly. Corner measures occurring for four intervals: {p_2} (1(A) = 1(B)), {p_2, p_3} (L->R), {p_3, p_4} (R->L), {2 x p_3} (middle-out); union conditioning regions can move corners off the junctions (corner-calculus).

cards.title: S10's circle model: the ultraviolet taper suppresses theta by ~20%, and there is no taper-free limit
cards.statement: Mechanism of the 0.300 vs 0.384 discrepancy. (1) In the NS-circle model of S10 Sec 7 the smoothstep taper on the spectral derivative (window uv in units of L; the Nyquist and the grid's second Fermi point both sit at |nu|/L = 0.5) damps exactly the ultraviolet modes near the moving endpoint where G_* lives. At L=256, a=2, Lg=1: theta = 0.27762, 0.28958, 0.36178, 0.72688, 0.54681 for uv = (0.20,0.32), (0.30,0.42), (0.35,0.47), (0.42,0.49), (0.46,0.499), and 0.17175 with no taper. The sweep is NOT a one-parameter scan: the first three windows share a transition width 0.12, and at that fixed width theta rises monotonically as the taper is relaxed at every L in the file (L=512: 0.28986, 0.29511, 0.32313; L=768: 0.29569, 0.29898, 0.31573); the last two have widths 0.07 and 0.039, and their theta = 0.72688, 0.54681 are artifacts of the sharp transition, not taper-strength data (REF-P0-TAPER). (2) There is NO taper-free limit: without the taper the periodic grid's second Fermi point (nu = +-L/2) doubles the Fermi sea and |u|^2 with it, 0.00739 -> 0.014889 (ratio 2.016), reproducibly in L (0.014889, 0.014912, 0.014921 at L = 256, 512, 768) with theta stuck at 0.17175, 0.19652, 0.20822: the untapered model is STABLE, it simply solves a different problem. Moving the taper's upper edge onto the second Fermi point at fixed transition width does the same (uv = (0.38,0.50): |u|^2 = 0.024005, theta = 0.56798). The |u|^2 = 0.02731 and 0.62691 of the two narrow windows are a separate, transition-sharpness (Gibbs) artifact, NOT the second Fermi point: at the same upper edge with a wider transition the norm is healthy again (uv = (0.25,0.49): 0.007628, theta = 0.36040; uv = (0.09,0.49): 0.007404, theta = 0.30780) (REF-P0-TAPER controls). So the taper is necessary AND it biases theta downwards; S10's window (0.30,0.42) is the safe one and its theta lies below the taper-free value at every L measured; a wider-transition window that passes the same gate more comfortably, uv = (0.25,0.49) (transition width 0.24, |u|^2 3.3% off against the 4.7% for which S10 discards (0.35,0.47)), already gives theta = 0.36040, the taper-free same-mesh value (no superlative is claimed: (0.09,0.49) has a wider transition still and a better norm, 0.007404, but damps the mid-band and gives 0.30780). (3) Proof that the MESH is not responsible (that the taper is the cause is (1)): running the modular Galerkin functional (exact vacuum symbol in closed form, exact continuum defect kernel, no taper, no cap) on the CIRCLE MODEL'S OWN MESH -- cells whose edges are the xi-midpoints of theta_j = 2 pi j / L mapped by xi = log((x+a)/(Lg-x)), x = tan(theta_j/2) -- gives theta = 0.34058, 0.35830, 0.36904, 0.37534, 0.37893 at L = 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048, i.e. the Galerkin values, at the same |D| and the same geometry where the tapered circle model gives 0.291, 0.290, 0.295, with |D| = 31, 63, 127, 255 on both sides; and the endpoint cap is not doing the work, since extending it to xi_max = 8.81, 20.81, 260.81 moves theta 0.35830 -> 0.35922 -> 0.35938 -> 0.35938 and saturates (f3_mimic_deep.out). (4) Consequently S10's Richardson in 1/L is also misapplied: the tapered theta_circ rises linearly in log L (theta = 0.28958 -> 0.30173 from L = 256 to 1024; d theta/d log L is flat at 0.0095-0.0096 over L = 512..1024, 0.0094 over 384..1024, and 0.0088 across the quoted endpoints), so continuing that trend to 0.384 would need xi_max ~ 14.8, L ~ 5e6 -- which is a reductio, since a law linear in log L is unbounded and cannot converge to 0.384 at all. S10's proofs P1-P5 and the qualitative conclusions DRAWN FROM theta > 0 ((S) fails, the compression is not the second-order minimiser, E^(2) <= (1-theta) f2 z^2) stand and are strengthened: 1 - theta = 0.616 +- 0.003 instead of 0.70. What does NOT stand is S10's own N2, 'ultraviolet-taper independent', and its verdict box's stability 'in L ... in the ultraviolet taper' (sdp_dual_certificate.tex l.861-863, l.911-913); and N3's non-perturbative 0.705 is a consistency check of the tapered model, not a measurement of 1 - theta.
